Question: Is it considered rude to expect a gift from guests at your birthday party?
Answer: It is not rude. People bring gifts to please you. It is part and parcel of the birthday party to get gifts, bouquets from others and money, gift cheques from elders with blessings. Some know you will wish them likewise on their birthdays. Because nowadays nobody has time for others. At the most a Whatsapp message or an involuntary birthday wish because Face book reminded them is all that happens. What if there is no party or any invite on their birthdays ? So you wish them anyway without fail , go to their place and surprise them with gifts and cake. Another way to accept gifts without any guilt is to give them a grand feast on your birthday, either lunch or dinner after the cake cutting snack party. This equals somehow. But nowadays I see most people giving away “return” gifts to guests, their children for attending birthday parties as a thankful gesture . This ensures the guests are pleased when they return. Besides the host is not obliged or burdened in any way if the guests or their children do not celebrate their respective birthdays. Not only that sometimes you may be unable to attend their invites. I feel this is the best thing to do. Now return gifts, gifts for the special “ occasion” as a memory are given to guests attending weddings, engagement functions, festival days, graduation parties, company get togethers, office promotion parties, house - warming functions etc. This is a quick way to return the favour and guests are happy too. 28.8.24.

Question: How do I move on after my husband died and I have found out he was having an affair?
Answer: You feel happy that he “deserved” to die and get lost from this beautiful universe..forever. A friend of mine was at that time 40 and her husband 46 when he suddenly died of cardiac arrest. They were both in government ( of India) jobs hence could afford multiple servants and helpers. We could have only a day - maid while they had maids, cook, watchmen, baby sitter and driver. When her husband was officially transferred he got himself a cook, an okay looking lady with a son of 13 years studying and staying in student’s hostel. So the cook stayed in his house ! First red flag. When he got transferred back to hometown he brought the cook along, ( 🚩) but accommodated her outside as my friend objected to the cook’s services and stay. 🚩 He died suddenly. I went for the funeral. What surprised us was the wife, that is my friend was quite calm., not shocked with his death. On the contrary she was pacifying us talking philosophy ! I felt something wrong in this approach. No shock, no tears, no fears of future for herself and her daughter. Only later we found our that the cook cried more, she worried more about the future of her son and herself leaving many guests surprised. Days after his death we realized my friend ‘s husband was having an affair with his cook. Some funeral guests, relatives even commented “isn't the cook more beautiful than the wife ?”. Probably they knew or understood or heard words between her wails. Moving on is very easy if the cheating husband dies. Better if you knew about it already. More happiness if killed by an accident at an young age . 26.8.24.

Question: What are some unique aspects of being an Indian grandchild, according to an Indian grandparent?
Answer: Our grand daughter in Sydney had some grading exam in her school, on 10th Aug this year, which checks the education level of the child . It is a common exam, not compulsory. We were then in India. As we video chatted with her she said “ thank god you are visiting Sydney after my exam “. When asked why she promptly replied “I can't manage two sets of people (her parents & grandparents) stressing me with this exam ”! So that's an Indian grandchild. The child is taught, cared, pampered, helped, protected and kept happy by parents and grandparents in the house, whether in India or abroad. Most grandchildren are very close to their grandparents. Grandparents are more like best friends for them where they reveal their whims, fancies, fears, thoughts, likes, dislikes, secrets and everyday happening without being judged or pulled up. Grand children get all their wishes full filled by grandparents. Some grandparents spoil their grand children with too much pampering too. Some grandparents are like influencerss, like heros whom the grandchild worships and follows. It is easier for a grandparent to convince a child into taking up a sport, a musical instrument, cycling or even eating healthy including all vegetables and fruits. Children growing up without grandparents lose out on something precious and often regret the vacuum. 25.8.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: Why have Indian girls almost stopped wearing sarees?
Answer: Not stopped but wearing it occasionally in marriages, festivals and community gatherings as in foreign countries. Only B and C town women are wearing them regularly. Why for that matter I am myself a person who reduced wearing sarees. First the convenience factor. Sari was never comfortable when I lived most of my working years in Ooty (Hill station). Once wet it remained wet until evening. I however wore to college, as a young bride and when working (school job). I looked good too. Otherwise it was salwar kameez, kurta - churidar for convenience and jeans- shirt kurta on Saturdays. Sari is not comfortable for daily wear by working women, travelling to and fro by bus, train etc. Sari is not comfortable for going on scooters, motorcycles and working in offices. Now it is now worn on office cultural days only. Saris are good for AC car travel and offices with AC due to global warming. Rising temperatures make sari - blouse very inconvenient. Cost.. Saree now costs more. Especially pure cotton and silk ones. What is worse is the blouse. Now stitching a blouse with trending embroidery costs atleast Rs1000 to Rs 5K. I stitch mine myself so no problem for me. Besides we women are crazy we do not repeat sarees to different functions even if they cost a lot. So sarees get piled up in the cupboards. Cost being too high we feel guilty donating them. Using saris for travel.. Indians are touring and travelling more. There are more tour agents now tempting family tours. Here saree takes a back seat. Most go for jeans, pants, Bermudas with tshirts, kurtas and long tops even senior citizens with shoes. After wearing dresses like tops, long frocks, since teen years girls, find it very uncomfortable wearing sarees where in we have a bit of our waist exposed and figure hugging blouse's left side too . Seniors like me are comfortable as that is how a sari is worn. I find many covering their left side with their sari pallu and ruining the outfit. Or some stitch blouses upto their hip! Sari is difficult to wear well unless you wear regularly. Most girls need others help and lots of pins. Now there is a ready to wear sari too, but it didn't pick much. Using wash room after wearing a sari ruins the sari pleats and folds completely. Especially starched cotton ones lose their shape. Carrying little children after wearing often tears the sari where it is pinned. Little children pull the pallus as they play around the mother. Sari needs good care and costly upkeep , ironing for cottons and dry clean for silk. Ten times the cost than other dresses, jeans, shirts etc Now sari with matching accessories has become like a fancy dress for occasional wearing, festivals, weddings, Tamil community gatherings and for NRI to fake patriotism and Indian culture. Nowadays many miss world and miss universe girls from western countries wear sarees as cultural outfits. My dil sells handloom saris online (all imported direct from Indian weavers) and sincerely advocates them by wearing it to all community gatherings in Sydney. But when it comes to convenience it is only faded jeans and T-shirts ! Saree is now only for sari lovers. Not for others. 25.8.24

Question: What are the reasons for some people to marry for wealth rather than love or affection? Is this considered morally wrong?
Answer: Love, affection, care, genuine friendships are needed in childhood, most of youth and the senior years. Last years of youth and middle age are usually the years of practicality. Here your survival is more important than love and affection. Many humans, not all, think smartly instead of morally in these years. That is why we see many marrying for wealth after breaking up with long time loving partners. The breakup is mutual with some good excuse and genuine reasoning. Sometimes it is abrupt too if the person is too smart and cunning. The break up is justified with excuses like parental pressure , society, difference in religion, other country, men still in university, men ‘s low income etc . But the main reason is jumping to a higher economic level through this marriage for a comfortable, secured life. Good Education also is a guarantee for better life as it promises good jobs, good salary and even migration to western countries. Is this considered morally wrong ? Yes, it is morally wrong to dump a long time bf /gf for money sake . You break promises, dissolve long term dreams and crash future plans with a person who trusted you. Why? All for the comforts of a wealthy life. You break their heart and make them lose trust in humans. You leave a wrecked person behind. So you are morally wrong, but practically right as far as survival on this planet is concerned. The person left behind also learns from this incident and becomes a smarter individual. After middle age the craving for true affection and love starts once again. So they start to look for it. If their spouse is the one, good for them. Others look for it in other women /men. We hear of fights, separation, abandonment, divorces , remarriage because of this want for true love which they once had in childhood and youth. It is a cycle. Lucky are those who get the same level of love, affection and care in all their ages.. childhood, youth, middle and old ages . 22.8.24.

Just when you want to relax and enjoy your retirement life, Life has other plans. My bil, a legal advisor for banks worked very hard, often stayed away from family on official transfers and when he retired at 60 to travel, to spend vacations abroad with his only daughter and lead a peaceful life in India, he died, abruptly at 60 years, 3 months. An outing, a vacation even a tour of 3-4 days takes out all the stress of this mundane life. Going to a place where they can loosen up is good for their body, mind and soul. I have been there often. Being a little dumb.. I am always too shocked and usually get frozen not knowing how to respond except for some facial reactions of shock or shame or “why me? ” . I take time because it is so sudden, it is embarrassing, there are people around and I am more controlled. Not responding is best. They do not get to see you in any ugly form. No words from you to requote you. Time heals?.. After that move away and give them time to retrospect. If they are good they will come back, sometimes feel sorry or ask for forgiveness. But many in my life have not comeback. Too guilty and ashamed, it was a easier for them to disappear from my life. Inspite of we extending our hand for a reconciliation they remain stuck and their super ego prevents them from making up. May be they lost all the love and trust in us. Even after years they are many still jammed blaming the whole past event on me . It is like “you caused it”. Immediate reaction?.. So first thing you do is to keep calm in such ugly situations. Move away for sometime. Time heals some. Some don't. Such relationships have reached a toxic level and would never want to get mended . Then you move on. Moving away, forgettin the incident, forgiving them is good for us. Long time reaction..Removing toxic relationships even if close ones is sometimes good for us. Be happy with the ones who remain. If nobody then too fine. Love yourself and be calm and happy. What matters ultimately is “ were you a good person and are you a good person ”. 11.8.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: Is it true about our Indian culture that on her wedding, a daughter is given everything she likes except the groom of her choice?
Answer: Groom is also her choice. She meets the groom. First sees the photo, then in person. Nowadays they talk for some time in the first meet alone without the other elders , then over the phone, go out often like dating , meet after work, message each other daily etc. Usually there is a gap of 3 to 8 months before they actually get married. So both have enough time to know each other and decide for sure. If the bride or groom is not happy the wedding is cancelled. Sometimes weddings are cancelled even after the betrothal function. Only in very few cases the parents choose the groom or bride and the adult children say “yes” to the person, trusting the parents’ choice. Here too most are educated enough, smart enough to contact each other through phones for knowing each other better. Now everybody has a cellphone right from 6th grade tuition going children! The problem arises if the groom is 10 plus years elder than the bride or it is second marriage for a man. If parents are very strict or they are against love marriage also this situation of forced marriage arises. Otherwise girls, boys in India choose to say “yes “or “no”. If nothing the groom or bride runs away from the wedding venue thus cancelling the wedding . Or if in love the lovers take refuge in police stations with proof of age and get married there ! India is changing. 9.8.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: If you have a mother and a wife, who is your 1st priority?
Answer: First priority wife, Second priority children, third parents.. Father and mother., then siblings, then his inlaws This is the order. But ask a man to answer honestly.. He will say he loves mother and his wife equally. Priority will change according to the situation and needs. Importance to one doesn't mean neglect the other. You don't choose between good mother and loving and a good wife, they are like parallel lines of a train track. They run parallel not touching each other but connected by those sleepers, fish plates and fasteners . They should remain equidistant throughout from each other for the smooth running of the train. Similarly both mother and wife are important for the man. He cannot choose one over the other. Both deserve equal love, importance and respect. He should ensure one doesn't overshadow the other nor does one act over possessive. He should ensure both women respect each other if not like or love. He should love them both equally but know the difference between love , responsibility for mother from the same for his wife. He should be part of both their lives. He shouldn't spend too much quality time with one at the expense of the other although now wife and children need and get more of his time. This is specially true where the son and family stay away from the son’s parents as nuclear family or in different towns, cities or even countries. Priorities to wife doesn't mean omission of mother from the man's life. Similarly a mil should remember a bride /son's wife is not a new maid for them to bully or spite. It is not difficult unless these three make things difficult. Mil and dil should maintain a healthy distance from each other and enjoy their space. They shouldn't interfere in each other's life unnecessarily . Even if one pulls the man too much to her side the man's life can tilt like a train jumping its tracks . 7.8.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: What is your one sentence when you wake up every day?
Answer: Nowadays when I wake up I say “another day today, I finished off one more day yesterday from my remaining quota, ”. Seems pessimistic, isn't it? At my age that is the truth. When young I never realized that we only live a fixed number of days on this earth. We used expressions like “ time is going so slowly in this physiology class “, or “it's boring at home, I wish vacations would go away fast” “time went away so fast this school term” “it is already time for exam “, “I wish we get vacations soon “, “I wish my birthday comes soon“ or“Wedding annv comes faster, or college reopens sooner “etc.. Not realising time flying away is time lost, our numbered days on this beautiful earth are getting over like we removing money from our savings. Every day is a subtraction from our total number of days. I feel my years flew away too fast in youth and middle age with a friends, education, home family, job, rest, sleep and social activities . Now with me in my early 60s I feel I'm scared I have only a few days left to do the things remaining, maybe to see more of the earth and it's beauty. To appreciate and enjoy whatever is there on this planet. I feel now the remaining days aren't enough. What if I have health issues? I know it is a negative approach. Suppose I live another 10 years (touch wood) that would be 10 x 365 days =3650 only .. That's all. That's too less.. I need more. That's why for me everyday is important now. Every day I need to spend it well. But each day spent means one day less from my fixed quota. So all of you use each of your days well. We have only a few days stay on this beautiful earth. Live it well. Do not let it slip away. Do not waste even a single day. 7.8.24.

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: How can we make waking up easier in the morning? What can we do before going to bed to ensure a more refreshed wake-up after a full night's sleep?
Answer: Have dinner before 8.00 pm. Include soups and fruits, thus including water in your diet. Avoid any caffeine drinks, cocoa products, drinks, cigarettes after 4 pm. Avoid exciting or disturbing videos, tv programs or reading crime novels before sleeping , Keep your smart phone far away on silent mode before going to sleep. These awaken your brain and won't let your brain sleep. Brain will not let your tired body to relax. Avoid phone calls before hitting the bed. Any conversation with people you love or hate disturbs your brain. You keep replaying the conversation in your mind . Sleep in comfortable clean bed with pillows of less height, fresh bed sheets. Change blankets, bed sheet atleast once in 7 to 10 days. Room temperature of 25 degree C is best for a good sleep. Solve all disagreements, fights etc with office colleagues, spouse, family, adult children before hitting the bed. Disturbed mind spoils sleep. Destress, be calm before sleeping. Avoid thinking over thinking and excitement. Meditate if know or just repeat “om “in your mind. Sleep in comfortable, loose cotton clothes. Remove jewellery, watch etc. Wash your face off any makeup, oil, sweat or dirt. Sleep in noise free dark room preferably or with a dim light. If you are not feeling sleepy , go for a stroll outside. Always sleep in the same room, same bed so that your body and brain both get tuned to the sleep routine. A good night's sleep ensures you get up every morning fresh like a lark. 6.8.24

Question: Why do people fear being alone even though they may be unhappy in their current relationships?
Answer: Many fear being alone inspite of being in an unhappy relationship because they fear multiple things at a time.. This is common in countries where education, career, new jobs available and economic levels are lower. This is more so in women of developing countries like India, Pakistan etc For them going back to parents is also a problem. Most parents get their daughters married off and do not want them coming back as singles due to social stigma. Many families do not want even widowed daughters back. One notorious example is Brindavan temple city in India where widows are brought and abandoned to fend for themselves by their own families . Most land in wrong hands. (sex racketeers) Getting out of unhappy relationships means starting a new one . Many prefer a known devil to an unknown angel. They get used to it and do not want to come out of this comfort zone. Moreover starting life once again with often a new job, new house, new town seems a tough job. If they have good savings it is easier to break up. Otherwise they feel it is better to continue in the current one they already got used to even if not very happy…as long as there is some money in hand, food, home and clothes. They literally give up on life and lead a monotonous life. The change scares them. For them everything else in life is fine for their happiness except their spouse /partner, which they sacrifice for sake of continuity, least disturbance in life and find fillup joys in other things like their children, jobs, daily entertainments, friends, partying, touring, hobbies, social life and social events. 6.8.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: What are your experiences at bunking class or school as an Indian teenager?
Answer: During my UG years in Ethiraj college chennai early 80s. We, girls a group of 7 decided to bunk classes and disappear one fine day. We were then in our final year. If not then we wouldn't be able to as our exams, were nearing. Our plan was to visit the zoo, children's park and reptile park. From there after lunch to go to the Besant Nagar beach and temple. All these places are near each other and most safe in Chennai besides having a good collection of restaurant for afternoon lunch. The fun part was in not informing our lecturers, tutors, classmates or hostelmates or anybody in the department. Just disappear and shock others. Our set was one of the most noisy and obvious ones with our good sense of dressing. We led the fashion parade in class! So our absence would be most felt. Two of us being hostelites started soon after breakfast and met the others at the Guindy zoo and Children's park entrance by 10 am. We enjoyed the zoo being science students. As we giggled and roamed around we were thrown our of our skin when we saw what we didn't want to see .. One of our class lecturers was standing there facing a tree and observing something. We were so engrossed in ourselves that by then we were a few metres away from her. In a split second we decided a U turn. But she turned in half a split second and caught us. We stood there embarrassed thinking what to say. We wanted to tell her not to tell our respective ward tutors about this bunking. As we desperately framed the sentences in our mind she smiled and asked us why we were here. We said that we took a day off to be together, one last time. She smiled, seemed fine and then she said “Don't tell anybody you saw me here”. We were pleasantly shocked, yet put on a standard smile. And she added “I'm doing my PhD research work on insects in tree barks. I haven't told any of the other staff members, I bunked college today. So Please DON'T tell others you saw me, okay? ”. We said yes ma'am in chorus and moved away quickly to let her do her work. We were so happy and relieved. Our bunking got neutraluzed by hers. Sometimes the universe also helps those in need . 😂 4.8.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: Where did you start learning how to cook, and did you learn alone or did someone teach you?
Answer: I started learning in our home science class in grade 9 in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. The Indian teacher taught us some basics like tea, rice, pooris, potato fry and potato fritters during the practicals besides house keeping tips…mid 70s Mid 80s…I learnt to cook first time with lots of fun and interest in our hostel while doing my PG. Our college and hostel were then closed down for 2 weeks due to some LTTE, Srilanka govt problem with after-effects in Tamil Nadu, India . All students were suddenly asked to vacate for security reasons. Everyone went home except those like me whose parents were abroad or north Indians whose native towns were far away. A few research scholars stayed back too to continue their lab work . But the hostel mess and college canteen were shut. We were left to manage on our own. Those days no smart phones or food delivery apps. Going out wasn't safe as we would be suspected of being LTTE cadres , Tamils of Srilanka hiding in TN, India ! Restaurant food wasn't hygienic or budget friendly. So we managed with bakery items, salads, fruits and pickles. A nearby tea shop was helpful for our morning coffee and evening teas and snacks. Soon a research scholar who stayed back brought an electric stove, some kitchen utensils, knives, cutlery etc from her guardian’s house. And we took the help of a kind hostel staff and secretly smuggled in basic groceries, vegetables as cooking of any sort wasn’t allowed. We cooked inside closed doors in our 1st floor room . It was fun cooking secretly sending the aromas through the back windows to the garden. We joked and giggled softly as we cooked . My senior taught me the basics as we juniors helped her with minor work like washing , cutting etc . We made rice, sambar, gravies, rasam some veg shallow fry. (only 3 items /day). Bought yoghurt, wafers and pickles too. Cooking was very basic with minimum ingredients, minimum work, no grinding, no deep frying, no pressure cooking, with bare minimum sound. We kept our radio on to drown the cooking tempering and sizzling sounds. Then we stealthily went to the mess to wash the used vessels. The whole secret process was exciting and the meal very tasty as we desperately longed for home food. This is where I learnt cooking with lots of fun, interest and the basics of my long innings in cooking, still going on… 3.8.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: Is it necessary to have expensive wedding rings for an arranged marriage between two people who have never met before?
Answer: Arranged marriage.. Two people who have never met or met just a few months ago. In Hindu religion there is no custom of rings exchanging initially. Only the groom is given a ring by his inlaws together with a gold chain and wedding suit. Soon we Indians started copying the western culture of rings exchanging by bride and groom. Now it is common ritual. It is not a must to have an expensive wedding ring if you cannot afford it. But a ring is considered a symbol of marriage, especially for others to know. A wedding ring exchanged by the groom and bride in front of their families, priest, guests as witness symbolises they are hence forth a married couple. These are only clear signs to show others they are not bachelors, singles. Some men even propose with a ring. If the girl accepts it means she is ready to marry him. Often rings are exchanged at the betrothal function also. Rings in fingers and toe rings (hindus) worn by women are nothing but a clear message to themselves and to others that they are now married, not single any more. They are committed to each other. All others do not try wooing us. Similarly it prevents people going astray, chasing others. Now the cost of the ring is dependent on the couple and their parents /families. Whether they can afford. Some can afford very costly diamond studded rings. For others rings are simple inexpensive ones. It is either made of platinum, gold or silver There are some couples who self buy rings , only after the marriage too. Rings are necessary, but needn't be expensive. 31.7.24

Question: What are some hair fall solution tips?
Answer: Have a balanced diet.. Include greens, mint leaves, fenugreek, spinach etc everyday. Have curry leaves as curry leaf - lentil powder with rice or kichidi. Have proteins daily atleast lentils, small fish varieties. Strengthen hair with coconut oil. Apply a little everyday. Avoid applying on the head, only on the hair. Applying oil stops hair ends splitting. Apply lots of coconut oil on hair strands and let soak for at least 2hrs before hair wash. This gives strength and dark colour. Oth erwise black hair fades to an unhealthy, dry brownish black. Do not apply too much conditioners as it smoothens hair, thins and weakens them. Preferably use organic shampoos or shikakai powder. Wash hair once a weak, not more, unless you have dandruff. Have vitamin B complex and iron tablets /capsules as supplements to your diet. Sleep atleast 7 to 8 hours everyday. Avoid unnecessary stressing over daily issues. Solve them or leave them to solve themselves. Ladies . Do not level hair often. Hair stops growing in length, unless you are born with good genes for thick, long hair. Those driving two wheelers.. Wear a head cloth before wearing helmets. Avoid cheap rough edge hair clips, tik tacs, butterfly clips etc . Buy higher quality smooth ones. 30.7.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: Why are people from India considered good at math?
Answer: Most of us are good in maths as all parents and school maths teachers lay lots of emphasis on maths. We are even promoted or retained by checking our annual Maths marks ! We have a Hindu god, lord Ganesha for helping us with Maths. And asked to eat slimy okra as it helps us with learning Maths. School children are discouraged from eating yam for the exact opposite reason. The only time we struggled in maths class is by age 6, 7 ( class 2, 3 ) wherein we are introduced to the mathematical tables from 1 to 12 . Maths teachers have a tough time making children mug up the tables. Some teachers who handled higher classes insisted we learn up to 20 tables . But most us dodged them but promptly learnt 13, 15 and 20th table and squares of numbers . Parents also check our math marks first then come the others like English, Science, social studies civic and languages. Our basic maths starts at home by our grand parents who trouble us with mental maths and grand mother who sends us errands to get various groceries from the nearby shop. We are forced to add, subtract mentally in the shop, check the bill and the return change, for fear of being sent back. I taught my son basic addition at his 2.5 years and later our grand daughter similarly while travelling long distance in car. I said we grand parents were giving candies separately and she was asked to total them using her fingers ! A good mark of 75 to 100 % in math means the child is intelligent. Whereas English and other languages with 55 % were easily okayed. Being good in maths ensures good marks in physics and chemistry too much needed in higher education, common entrance exams, college, university admission . Being good in maths is the first step to survival in India and the world for us. 29.7.24

Question: I got up at 10 minutes til nine in the morning and finished my breakfast after 9 am. What time should I be having my lunch?
Answer: You had breakfast say at 9. 15 am. Usually our stomach takes 3 to 4 hours to digest our food presuming it is a balanced diet that has balanced portions of carbs, fats, proteins, fibres etc. So adding 3.5 hrs to 9.15 equals 12.45. So you can eat lunch at 12. 45 to 1 pm Then tea time snacks with coffee /tea or milk at 4pm. And finally dinner at 7 pm to 8 pm. Senior citizens should have light dinner by 7pm, not later. 28.7.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: We are both married, he makes me happy and I have tried to work on my marriage with my husband but he doesn't care much, I am ready to keep it a secret, what do I do?
Answer: Both of you are married. Yet fell in love. This happens due to simple attractions, sweet interactions in place of work, suburb trains, travel to and fro office, with your pleasant neighbour, your old flame on fb or an ex bf and very often a distant relative. This is so true in middle age often called as midlife crisis which craves for opposite sex attention. It is very flattering to be in love once again. The missed heart beats, the rush of adreline, the daily meets, the sleepless nights etc are all mentally rejuvenating to you. You also tend to keep yourself physically fit and attractive suddenly. You suddenly find happiness and some meaning to life.. But beware all these are illusions like a mirage. Since your husband is not giving enough quality time you feel happy when someone gives you so much attention and speaks so kindly to you. But you cannot runaway from the reality of a husband, children, stable marriage and society. So you intend to eat the cake and keep it too. You want best of both worlds. It seems easy to keep it a secret and carry on this EMA behind your blind husband's back. But in reality it isn't. First it is fun. The thrill, the temptation is a mind blowing, happy feeling. You feel like a free teenager once again, getting pampered by her bf. But as soon as both your mental and physical needs are met you both fall back to reality. The person who realizes this first will try to avoid the other hereafter. Then starts the possessiveness fights , fight for more time, fight for gifts and other rights. Envy, jealousy, hatred anger, towards the spouse starts. You get hurt and sad. This leads to more arguments and fights with more avoidance from him /you. It can have extreme results including physically hurting each other, mental trauma, heart break suicide or one stabbing the other, whichever is easy. Let's presume you do keep this EMA a big secret but one day things go wrong. What if you are caught? Are you bold enough to face the shame, live through the guilt. What about facing your children who have high opinion about you? Do you want to live a happy long life OR get killed by someone or severely hurt by a scorned bf (think stabbing, acid attack, uploaded private moment videos, etc) . Choose yourself. 27.7.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: Is it morally acceptable to be in love with someone who is married but unhappy?
Answer: NO . No. No. It is NOT morally acceptable to love someone else's husband or wife. It is immoral. That is why extra marital affairs are considered unethical, indecent and anti social. Even if you are not married you should not fall in love with a married person. Even if you do, without knowing his /her marital status , back out immediately. If the other person also says he /she is in love with you then ask them to first divorce their spouse, then proceed in this love. Until then wait. They do not show off except that they live well in prime locations, buy hi end cars, mansions, private planes, cruise, islands and yachts for travel. Otherwise they were a grey t shirt and simple jeans. No watch only a smart phone, card as accessories. Unlike us poor Indians.. We had (still have) caste system which allowed only the upper castes and kings, queens families to show off their knowledge, power and wealth. Others like traders, farmers, tradesmen paid tax. I don't even want to write about the pathetic situation of lower middle, lower castes and tribal people. Some weren't allowed to cover their chests (including women ) and children sat on sacks instead of chairs and benches in schools! We were ruled by the British for 200 years who hyponitized us to think they were the masters, with super fair skin, stylish English, all the powers and we had to bend down like a question mark? and act humble, simple pathetic and toothless. We were also witness to zamindaars, nawabs, mirasdaars and likes who had a trail of managers, servants, clerks, maids, drivers, watchmen, cooks and other staff who were treated as lower humans . . . Now India has changed. In new India our economic levels have shot up. People are highly educated, earn well, many successfully run businesses and now the new rich feel we have a right to show off what we have earned. Unlike their parents or grandparents, great grandfathers who were then saluting the British, Portuguese, French masters or the Indian big shots like the maharajas, nawabs or rich “Nehru” like families. So for now we will show off till we get used to seeing plenty of wealth. Till we get bored of our prosperity. May be in a decade or half we will stop showing off. Already many are humble down south, inspite of being very rich. So until then tolerate Indians who show off. They have a right. You have a right to ignore them or feel happy for them. Feel happy India is changing economically. 23.6.24

Question: What are the emotions of an average Indian mother when she sees her child in a foreign country?
Answer: Our son worked for a good salary in Bangalore. He was happy and so were we. He worked long hours as expected in group work in IT fields. Ofcourse the Bangalore traffic made him come home late sometimes but weekends were holidays. Then he got transferred to Australia. Soon the parent company absorbed him in and he became a PR and then citizen . There the work culture was similar except that nobody worked after 5.30 pm. He has more family time. Enjoys cooking and gardening as a passion. He meets his friends too often. The environment there is cleaner, no traffic jam, more discipline everywhere and the place is closer to nature. I was happy he went abroad as life seems better there for youngsters . My dil is employed too and has a hassle free train travel everyday to the CBD, Sydney . She is active in the local Tamil community /social group. Has a small sari business also . Our grand child is growing up happy and confident in a multi cultural set up. We went there to stay with them. They are happy, we are happy for them. Our son's work / stay there, our grand child's studies , the world out there is clean, curruption free, disciplined traffic, neat suburbs filled with greenery is like a dream come true. The place abounds with beautiful birds everywhere and there are many, great, natural, unspoilt places for sight seeing. We travelling abroad is also a great event .. Planning, shopping, packing, travel, transit, stress free holidaying etc and then visiting nearby cities, countries enroute were all bonus for old people like me who are permanent residents of India ! We feel proud of our son and dil who have adjusted so well in a new, better country. We do wish we all could live together. But these are two different countries, two cultures and with a good age difference. So in all I would say it is a social prestige but a personal loss. But I feel it is okay for us to sacrifice a bit for their better lives. We have lived ours well, they should live theirs better. 👍 22. 6.24

Question: Why are Indian househelps so demanding and greedy?

Most employers retain old known maids than training an unknown new one. Cost of living is going up silently. Some day to day things like groceries, provisions go up every week. These price rises are never announced in the annual budget by the government. So they need a decent raise every year. They also have peer pressure like you. So need to buy new clothes, update phone, buy smart TV, scooters, smart watch etc. They need weekly holiday to rest or be with their family. They need festival holidays to enjoy with family and relatives. Their standard of life has gone up just like ours. So starting salary is high. Raise is 10 percent. One full salary as Diwali bonus. They expect good gifts for festivals, old hand overs should be in good condition. They will not wash clothes without a washing machine. They know their rights well and some are members of a maids union. 22.6.24

Question: Why do people in India think that startups are bad?
Answer: Start ups are good according to youngsters and those entering middle age. Youngsters, those in 30s are more adventurous. But all others who are elder than these dread start ups. They fear for safety of money over risks .They prefer neighbour’ s son taking risks but not their own adult children. They like praising their relative’s children as “great business men” but their own children should have a decent, safe job like a government job or a high paying IT job. In fact getting brides for business groom is very difficult than a man with a secure 9 to 5 job. Start ups have a history of failures mainly because the starters are impatient, inexperienced youngsters with dad’s money. Almost 95 % fail or the successful ones had atleast three severe losses draining energy and money. But those who invested self earned money , have experience in that field seldom fail. They succeed with hard work and working knowledge. A good example is my husband. After a good experience in mushroom cultivation in HLL (Unilever) he started his own business in the same field. He had two partners, who were also experts in button mushroom. My husband was then 45 years of age. His partners a few years younger. And they did well too. He earned more than his 15 years as an employee in HLL. Indians prefer a safe life. Hence they quickly deposit money in FDs in govt banks, post office, PPF etc and in long term mutual funds or stable long term shares . BUT they think twenty times, when pouring lakhs of money as capital for a new business or pledging properties for new ventures or their inexperienced, adult children. Our friend’s son works in Reuters (bangalore). . He is an engineer. After 5 years he saved enough, pooled Rs 6 lakhs with three others and started a “ food kitchen “ and a delivery app . Within a year they burnt their fingers and closed down the business. He is now happy working for Reuters as before. It was his own earnings that he lost. So Indians prefer working for others as this is a safer way out, more stable for life. 20. 6. 24.

Question: What is the life expectancy of an apartment in Chennai?
Answer: Around 50 years plus or minus 5 years depending on the quality of its construction. We had an apartment in Chennai. It was in a prime area of Nungambakkam. Bought it in 1988, our first purchase on an office loan, cost Rs 3.5 L. We used it for 4 years when son and I stayed there for his very crucial 9th to 12th grade school education. After that only tenants stayed there. Our apartment wasn't taken care of by the numerous tenants. It looked pathetic with stained kitchen, washrooms and termites eating away wooden doors, leaking pipes. This is inspite of regular repairs and full professional cleaning, painting and acid washing of bathrooms whenever tenants changed. The last tenant was the worst of them all. Finally by 2018 we wanted to dispose it. By now it was 30 years old. There were many proposals to sell , demolish the full sixteen apartments and rebuild with each owner getting a new apartment and the builder getting a whole new floor added. But many owners refused to shift out fearing the usual delays in construction. Some were old and weak. My professor is an owner there. Meanwhile our flat fetched only a pathetic price of Rs 54 L maximum. We felt bad seeing our first purchase in such a dilapidated condition. It needed a complete rejuvenation. We owed our dear house this. So we changed the bath tiles, accessories, floor tiles, doors, all closets, got it painted . Now it looked brand new. Immediately we got a buyer for Rs 70 L. Luckily the construction quality of the pillars, columns of the 80s was good. People are still living there and will continue for another 15 years easily. 16.6.24

Question: Which one is the right question, "You liked it" or "Did you like it"?
Answer: Which one is the right question, "You liked it" or "Did you like it"? Presume “ I liked it.” is the answer to a question. Let's change this to its question form. “ Did you like it ?” this is most appropriate interrogative form of the answer sentence given above. . You liked it? ( said with a pull in the words or with lots of head nodding) In colloquial English many use this format to ask the same question “ You liked it ? ” This is a wrong sentence. It is a declarative sentence with a question mark. A hybrid of declarative and interrogative sentences. Actually it is an incomplete sentence. The sentence needs a question tag. So it should be “ You liked it, didn't you ?”. 15.6.24

Question: What would you like to cook in the rainy season?
Answer: Bhajias (fritters). Usually potato, if well prepared with jalapeños or plantain . Every rainy season there is one day when the clouds gather as if in a hurry and turn a 14.30 to a dark silent evening like it were 18.30. As we lie on the bed not sure whether the clouds, would clear up or stay .. it pours starting with huge drops drumming on asbestos sheets . Thud, thud, thud. Then the rain waters splash windows and there is heavy rain, hand in hand with the strong wind. They seem like best friends meeting after a year, screaming with joy . This is the moment I get up and head to the kitchen. I pour oil in the kadai. Mix in the bajji batter and get slices of a big potato. I make it spicy as the rain gives us a right to fried, spicy food. Meanwhile I keep the vessel for getting the tea ready. Both done. We go to the hall with tomato sauce and the Indian mint chutney. We have the fritters hot, crisp yet melting in our mouth and drench them down with hot tea. Wow what a combination.. Dark day, Rain, wind, bhajias and tea. 15.6.24

Question: Can a person live his whole life without getting married?
Answer: Yes. Why not ? My friend is not married although she could have. She belongs to Vellore, Tamil Nadu. She is happy living her life like she wants. 15.6.24.

Question: Is there a formula for achieving perfect happiness in life? Can everyone attain true happiness through effort?
Answer: Yes.. By contentment and detachment from world, people, family etc . I am trying. Contentment is easier. But detachment I can't. Try them may be you can. How much ever effort I put in I can't .. Contentment leads to happiness. Good. But what about the torture we are subjected to by others. We live in a society which keeps trying us out. Can we say I'm contented and happy in spite of so and so hurting me, cheating me, insulting me ? Our society isn't completely good. When I'm happy for some days invariably there is a visitor or a phone call or a news that makes me unhappy/angry /perturbed/causes anxiety . Even the fact that I say “I'm happy today, no worries or bad thoughts “ only means, I'm not worrying right now. It is not that every issue got resolved, all insults taken back or all hurts vanished. Because they don't. They are hidden or dormant temporarily. Or a new happiness over shadowed the old sorrowful ones. Even a thick skinned person is tortured as he /she endures . The only way to perfect happiness is by CONTENTMENT and by mind control that is no disturbance by or remaining neutral to both HAPPY or SAD events. This is possible by being detached and neutral to worldly acquired things like family bonds, material wealth and our uncontrolled thoughts. We must erase all old files in our mind. Keep the mind empty and open. Let thoughts, come and go freely. Let nothing stay inside to ponder. Some people do stay happy forever like our saints. Nothing insults them, nothing hurts them. They do not chase anything. They are happy and contented. They go into a state of complete detachment from everything. That is why many go to far off places like Himalayas. Some ordinary people too go away far from society to forests, hillsides, grasslands set up simple self sustaining homes near water sources and live alone leading simple lives . They too are happy. This is common in western countries. The so called saints in making even change costume to become a new person with no attachments to their past . I heard many resort to drugs to forget the world and old issues they escaped from . (drugs are available easily in himalayan temple towns and villages) . Can you leave everything and go ? I need lots of guts to do that. I can't. I need company, I need family. Besides I still have old issues to solve. Can't forget them so easily. Can't live peacefully without seeing the judgement the world gives . So we can't until we are compensated the mental agony, the unfair treatment and the advantage the world took of us. Many of us have gone through this. Some of us forget these in busy lives. But the thoughts come back when mind is idle especially in old age. It is like the world owes us an explanation only then our mind will get calm and peaceful. Old files need to be erased. We humans can then be truely happy. Or leave everything by cultivating utmost detachment. Stop thinking and overthinking. Be calm. Find true happiness. It is all around. No need to go to the Himalayas or live hidden from the world in thick forests. No need to take alcohol or drugs. As we age we find contentment , we do control these itchy thoughts and forgive our offenders but we aren't fully successful. It takes great voluntary effort to do this and become completely blissful. At that stage nothing disturbs us physically or mentally. We are then really HAPPY. 14.6.24

Question: Is it common for Indian parents to expect their children to become doctors or engineers if they study well?
Answer: Yes. Usually doctors, engineers, lawyers, CA , then pursue IAS, IPS etc if you are still not satisfied. This is mainly because they will get good jobs, earn well and lead comfortable lives. Parents cannot be fending for their adult children life long. So this is the easy way out. If their life is already comfortable with profitable family businesses or their father is a famous actor or powerful, smart politician etc then they can choose all other professions, whatever they like. Nowadays everybody completes a minimum of graduation so getting jobs is becoming very difficult. There is high competition in white collar and blue collar jobs. We have heard of 50K people applying for a single govt job vacancy ! The situation is so pathetic that sometimes even PhDs are applying for sweeper jobs in Indian government sectors. So your type of education is very important. A profession degree has more value. Jobs, salary, self employment, entrepreneurship come next. Otherwise all normal people strive to get a good education for career sake and keep their passions as hobbies and follow both simultaneously. It is thus a win win situation. 12.6.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: Do Hindu grooms see their brides before they get married?
Answer: Most do. Earlier they didn't if it was an arranged marriage between newly introduced families. Or the alliance was through a common matrimonial broker. Usually photos were exchanged, without knowing the actual height, weight and character of the person. But if it was between known families, close relatives or far away relatives, invariably the eligible bachelors and brides to be met in temple functions, village festivals, fetes weddings etc. Many thus fell in love before marriage and got the marriage arranged with the help of parents, grandparents, uncles, aunts etc. Later the practice of the arranged marriage went one step ahead and let the two talk to each other, go out after engagement function too. Now it too easy as both have cell phones, exchange phone numbers, have enough freedom to go out together or with company (call them dates). I'm completing 40 years of married life. Ours was an arranged marriage, families unknown to each other except that a far away relative was one of the dils in this house. Since I stayed in the college hostel and my parents were then abroad I found it easy to go out , (rather slip out without parent’s permission) with my future husband so as to know him better. If my parents were in India they wouldn't have allowed me . Otherwise getting married to a stranger and seeing his face only in the marriage hall and Pooja, /homam stage wasn't okay with me at all . I needed to see, speak with him to know whether I could adjust with that newly introduced human. After all it is a long term contract of togetherness. But even now in many backward places especially in some villages in northern and western parts of India we do hear of grooms and brides seeing each other for the first time only on the wedding day. But the parents would have seen, chosen and approved them. What if the parents choice doesn't match the adult child's? It can be disastrous. Or a life long compromise or like nowadays they break the marriage run away with some fb /insta friend. Some even migrate to other countries for the new lover . Better to see, talk, understand each other before marriage otherwise there is every chance to say “ No “ at the altar or disappear at night a few days before the wedding. 12.6.24.

Question: What do we do when we are feeling low? Should we pamper our sadness or should we go for something more cheerful?
Answer: I am often woken up by worries and negative thoughts. They seem overpowering. On such days I get out of the house without fail, go for a walk. I try my best to forget these low feels but they control me. Then I give myself strictly 5 more minutes to worry and voluntarily put a full stop on these low feelings. Sometimes I even end up saying “OK shut up, that's enough” to my worrying mind and feel lighter. I follow these whenever sad, hurt or negative thoughts overpower me. Try them, you may get benefitted too in any of these. If you are feeling low first get out of closed rooms. Get out of the house. Go for a walk. Go to the park, sit on the benches there and watch greenery all around. See the birds, sky, clouds etc Pamper yourself with good tasty food. Preferably fried snacks. Fats make us happy, so does milk shake. Even a good coffee would boost your energy. Buy yourself clothes if you have time. New clothes, accessories make us happy . For some time mind gets diverted and soon we forget our worries. Or go for a long drive to some quiet roads surrounded by greenery. Forget all your worries with good lively or romantic songs, not sad songs. Or talk to your friend. Most friends talk a lot. You just listen. It will calm your mind. If you have a pet dog play with it or look at swimming fish in your aquarium. . . Kill your low, sad feelings. Do not let them control your life. No point worrying. I always overpower my sad thoughts with a change in thoughts. 👍 10.6.24

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: Is it necessary to tell your spouse about a past affair, even if it is no longer ongoing and they are unaware of it?
Answer: No. It is not necessary. But failed elopement, broken engagements, broken marriages should be told. All other break ups, crushes, loves, affairs before engagement and before marriage needn't be spoken of. This is for both men and women. Keep it a secret and take it to your grave. Why? Actually two families got married . But now there is more mingling of youth. They meet, get friends of both sexes, become close and often go on to married life successfully. The stigma of love marriage is not there. Here all other criteria do not matter much as parents try. Even horoscope is avoided and they are left to themselves (fate) . Media, online exposure has also shown people better choices are there in life. Break ups are common, even celebrated. No depression . Both move on, part even as friends. They compete with each other and find the next friend. Similar to throwing nets to get the best catch. There are so many choices both at national and international levels. So going for arranged marriages inspite of family support, wealth support is like a blind folded person walking into a dark room to look for their life partner. Don't know who the spouse really is behind the smiling mask, how many trippings on the dark floor, how many dashes against the walls before he /she meets their spouse. Not everyone is lucky to find their loving spouse in the shortest time and distance in such dark rooms. Love marriage is like entering a well lit, AC room, walking on a clean floor to a loving known spouse. Unless ofcourse the whole love was fake and only for benefits. 1.6.24.

Question: What practices are strictly forbidden inside temples in India?
Answer: There are many rules to be followed in Hindu temples.. Many of these apply to Buddhist, Jain temples and Gurudwara too. Cleanliness is very important. Do not enter if your are not clean physically and mentally. Keep the temple premises clean. No soiling, oiling or leaving ash, kumkum on temple pillars, floors, premises. Keep your footware out of temples , iPad cellphone switched off. Wear decent clothes. No showing of body below knee and sleeveless dresses not allowed. Some temples (thirupathi ) have strict dress code, follow them. No romance in the temple premises. No touching of woman /men in queues, no flirting, no pushing. Temples are not places for entertainment or tussle . Do not break queues. Do not dirty or scribble on temple walls pillars. Do not light camphor as it darkens temple walls and roofs. Do not put number markings, exam roll no.,lines etc on walls. Outside food is not allowed. If eating temple prasadam, coconut, bananas laddus etc eat without spilling and dispose the leaf - cup away, paper cups in the dustbin. Wash hands in the tap water. Always circumnavigate the temple in clockwise direction. Prostrate only below the main post of the temple found in the temple compound near the entrance . Nowhere else. Always sit for some time in the temple premises, in the corridors or verandahs before leaving. (otherwise the demigods, saints may come home with you). Do not pluck temple flowers, leaves, baby plants, fruits or seeds. Keep silent as much as possible. No chatting, chattering, screaming or calling out to each other or gods loudly. Do not pray if the Garba graha curtains are put and the god is getting dressed, decorated for darshan . Do not go to temple if your are menstruating, without a bath after se£, for a month after baby delivery, after haircut (salon visit), if there is a contagious sickness in your house, village, the town or city, if there was a funeral in your house /extended family in the last 11 /13 days. 25.5.24

Question: Which traditional color cloth is best for going to a Hindu temple?
Answer: All colours are allowed nowadays. Earlier black wasn't appreciated as it denotes bad luck and sorrow. But now black is a trending colour. Out of 20 people in a temple, 15 are in black dresses, shirts and often with blue or black jeans etc But traditional colours are.. Orange, all reds, maroon, sunset yellow, light yellow Followed by light orange, peach, pink, magenta, purple, The next in the line are white, light green, baby pink, pastel, light blue,, light grey, lavender . The last in the line are the dark colours like navy blue, black, bottle green, dark violet and dark brown. Why these colours? Probably because the bright colours are preferred especially in silks.. Sarees, shirts and dresses. Silk is worn as a norm when visiting temples and on festival days. In fact traditional weavers do not have black silk at all , only the darkest shade of green is given as black ! Black colour brings bad luck even to the weavers. according to them. During festivals, rituals and poojas we use lots of turmeric, sandal paste and kumkum. Sandal paste has a stubborn brown stain. These are yellow, brown and red respectively and easily stain our clothes if spilt on our sarees and dresses. Hence devotees prefer red, dark orange and yellows sarees, clothes for temple poojas, homams, gruha pravesh pooja, baby first food morsel ceremony etc. Many men who wear white silk shirts, dhotis usually get it stained in remembrance of that function. Early days with no electric lights the Garba-Graham (the central, main room where idol is kept and pooja done everyday) used to be lit only by oil lamps. So idols looked good only in bright silk colours.The idols are all dressed in bright colours since then especially our goddesses.. Ammans (Shakthi), Lakshmi, Saraswathi, Durga etc so we presume we should also be in the colours she likes. Dark colours are not clearly visible in the dark parts of the temple when we go around each single sub-temple. Similarly when we circumnavigate around the main temple compound. Many temples do not have lights at the back part of the temple compound . Some have dim lights at corners. So imagine someone in black dress jump down suddenly from the back yard peepul tree, rahu - ketu assemble, raised platform. 😩 I prefer orange, maroon and yellow. I usually wear yellows to Vishnu temples. I avoid black to temples and during travels . But like I said nowadays all colours are allowed in temples and black is trending. But wear decent clothes to temples, after all you are going to see your respected god. Avoid dirty, stinky clothes especially polyester ones. 22.5.24

Question: How can one provide assistance to elderly parents who refuse outside help and are resistant to moving from their home or living with their children?
Answer: Many parents live alone in their own houses unable to shift to the houses, towns, cities and places abroad where their children work or do business. They dread shifting out of known places as they are so used to neighbours, neighbourhood and their houses, rooms and gardens too. A known town, city and country is a blessing too when you retire and want a stress free life. The ease of living in one's own home is heaven compared to the best of hotels and choices of services . I am a good example of such a senior citizen. Shifting out from a well settled house is literally like uprooting a delicate plant and replanting elsewhere in unknown conditions. Only strong plants can survive such transfers . So how do adult children of such senior parents live guilt free, stress free ? How do they take care of such parents? . . Call or message everyday just to keep in touch of their well being. Video call atleast once a week. Visual calls speak more than audio. You can track their health. Many parents hide their health issues from children who live far away. Keep in touch with parents ‘ neighbours too for help in any emergency . Keep in touch with relatives for any big issues or emergency. Transfer money if they are in need. My friend lives alone in palakaadu, Kerala after her husband passed away. She has a day - maid. Her son visits her every month, he lives in Bangalore. He pays all her bills online..groceries, provisions, amazon shopping, medicines and is present for her regular doctor visits . If needed fix a good, trust worthy, full -time servant for house care, for their assistance especially very old, weak parents. If needed arrange a cook to make simple senior- friendly, fresh meals or arrange daily delivery of hot food. Payment can be done monthly. Make their washroom senior friendly with handles in walls, slip proof tiles, mats, good lights etc. Keep their medicines in reach and never delay buying of essential medicines and taking them to doctor for check ups. Get them BP, oxygen level, blood sugar measuring kits, for checking regularly. Arrange for an annual or biannual blood test. Be with them for as many gatherings as possible with their grand children. Birthdays, festivals, family weddings, extended family gatherings, annual gatherings should be made enjoyable occasions for them. Take them on tours every year or once in 6 months to places they like and has comfortable weather and terrain . Make such trips a happy occasion for everybody not namesake trips to post pictures on instagram . Give them genuine company whenever you can, not compulsory attendance. 20. 5. 24

Question: What is the best old temple to visit in Chennai?

It is an ancient, lord Krishna (Vishnu avtaar) temple built the 6th - 8th century by the Pallavas rulers ( emperor Narasimha varma Pallava I laid the foundation ) , then renovated, expanded by the Cholas and later by 11th to 15th century resurrected by emperor Krishnadeva Raya (Vijayanagara dynasty ). The temple entrance Here Krishna is worshipped in his super - human sized idol which sports a prominent moustache. Krishna idol in the form of a sarathy or charioteer as in Mahabharata. Thus he has no weapons. The idol has numerous wounds as he is hurt in the war. moustache on his war wounded face.. Partha with his consort Rukmini and brother Balarama Parthasarathy Temple is a splendid spectacle featuring striking shrines of Lord Narasimha, Sri Yog Narasimhar, Lord Gajendra Varadar, Lord Chakravarthy Thirumagan, Lord Ranganatha, Goddess Vedavalli and Goddess Andal. It also enshrines Hanuman, Swami Manavala Mamunigal and Vedanthachariar. Krishna is present in the Garbha Gruha along with his consort Rukmani, brother Balarama, son Pradyumna, grandsons Anirudhha and Satyaki. The temple has a beautiful big gopuram, a temple pond and huge compound walls. The lanes around are good for walking through and for auto rickshaws but not for cars in width. The houses are all old, built long ago for priests and people who worked in the temple. I have gone there often as it was just a 10 minutes walk from Presidency college, where I did my M.Sc. Question: What made you believe in God? Tell me your experience.

At that time we owned 4 apartments.. in Chennai, 2 in Coimbatore and Ooty. Bought with savings from Unilever job. Then my husband quitting his regular job, started his own business.. Button mushroom farm in Ooty. All thanks to our business partner (most useless, work evading) we were forced to relocate to a small village (Annur) to correct the failing business. We shifted into an upper floor, decent house for rent on the highway. (far from village - town centre) . My husband took over the compost making, spawn culture and mixing in compost before sending the bags for growing. Meanwhile our partner shifted to Ooty to take care of the mushroom growing and sales. The place was a complete contrast to cities and towns, a true village in all senses . Drinking water had to be carried to the first floor from the common tap down. I was asked to sweep and draw rangoli in the common entrance down every second day. Getting maids was very difficult . But we adjusted for our business sake by getting an AC fixed in the house and buying an UPS for power cuts. Tamil Nadu was those days notorious for 8 hours of power cuts /day ! Inspite if all these I enjoyed the village life, fresh air, the beautiful birds, ancient temple, weekly market and simple life. Soon the farm ran well. Profits poured in, but business partners lost trust in each other. After 2 years of good profits, paying loans on time we wanted to move out by selling all our shares to our partner itself . He promised to pay us before Sep '12. Like decent people we informed the house owner 3 months ahead about us shifting out. He immediately got a new tenant with higher rent. House owner started torturing us to vacate and we had no place to shift as it was a village with most houses, even huts occupied. We even checked empty garages and godowns! Finally my husband decided to stay in a hotel nearby on monthly rate and I to shift to our house in Ooty, hoping our partner relieves us soon. We packed our things into card board boxes to shift out in two days on the 17th of Jan 2013. I thought we were so desperately pushed for a house to stay inspite of having 4 of our own . Cannot continue in the farm as partners have fought.. But forced to continue till money reaches our account. As I felt the burden of pressure, shame and desperation.. I didn't even think of god or temple. I was busy thinking of us, humans only and how to bravely manage the situation. God's act.. As we packed on 15 th Jan, our tv cable person came home to enquire about us leaving. I told him we were leaving because we couldn't find another house here. He immediately said a house nearby got vacated the previous day and he could get us that. We said OK not even checking the house , only trusting him. A few phone calls and on 17th Jan ‘13 we shifted into this house. A small one with fresh water tap as usual outside. No car park, the same power cuts etc. With only borewell supply inside. We shifted. It was a lucky house. Our partner gave us all the due money by February '13, our son’s marriage got fixed and we vacated this house in April 13, in just 4 months. Question: What is a life lesson that parents may not want their children to learn on their own?
Answer: From our life experience.. The use (misuse) of credit card. Our son was then a few years into earning with a job in IT field, good starting salary . He sent monthly 5K home as I asked him. But it wasn't regular. Remaining went away in rent, food, gadgets, Internet, travel etc in Bangalore. He shared an apartment with his friends. Soon the sending home money became more irregular. He was buying new smart phone, multi lens camera, play station, joined a gym, new TV, a pet dog, fridge etc. At 25 he bought his first car .. A small one, i10 hyundai. He was advised this as a motorcycle was a precautionary “No”. When we relocated to Bangalore in 2013 we took a part-loan on his name for our new flat, rest paid by us. When we went for loan the LIC manager asked him to clear all his office and citibank loans to get LIC loan approved. Instead of telling us the details of his loan he was always lost in deep thoughts. Sometimes angry with everyone. I slowly asked him once and he told he had a big loan to pay back. We were shocked to a see a fat Rs 4 lakhs (400, 000) in his name. Until then he kept us blind and out of it. All these because of over spending on high end gadgets , ‘away from parents’ life style etc.. And thus over borrowing from the daily calling, ready to give, kind bank. When my husband came to know of it our son felt very ashamed and got a few lessons in spending, borrowing, debit and credit cards. Anyway we paid all his loan and the LIC loan was started fresh. Our son paid the monthly EMI for 5 years and then we repaid it completely by the 6th year itself whenever we had cash . It is now 2024. He has become very responsible and lives with his family in Sydney managing earnings and expenses better . Some lessons are learnt like this. It is better they are taught before adult children get into trouble. 18.3.24

Question: Can one live happily without social media?
Answer: Yes, yes, yes. We went to New Zealand from Sydney on a 5 days tour (with one day more gone for flights and time difference) . I wanted a break from all social media including Google search, news, maps, WhatsApp, telegram, Quora, Fb. I'm not on Instagram, X and other apps. It was like a real vacation, taking a break from others except family members who were with me .. Husband, son, dil and granddaughter. My tickets, visa and hotel reservations were in paper printouts. Besides nowadays passport has all the information needed just by scanning them in airports. Things are now so easy and transparent. I used my phone only as a camera. Didn't carry any iPad too. Just one 9 by 9inches handbag to carry the camera - phone, some mint and tissue. That's all. No burden like all others who had shoulder bags! It was peaceful all the 5 + days. My friends and extended family knew we were away for 5+ days so no worries or searching me as “missing person” . I enjoyed nature at its best. I gained time. I had no delays. I had no neck pain or shoulder pain. I enjoyed the tour. This is not the first time I did this kind of escape. I do that often whenever on tours, both inland or abroad. Besides nobody believe me, is interested in your tour photos. So humility helps in getting full happiness. No expectations for likes , no comments, no snubs, no fake praises, no criticisms, no anxiety means absolute peace. Try it. It is so relaxing, having time all for yourself is a boon. 18.3.24

Question: Since years I’m trying to get that happy and satisfied person I used to be with no success. Everything has become so grey and lifeless in my life and I’m functioning because I have to in order to survive. Which advice can you give me to get better?
Answer: The other day I read an article by a famous psychologist and philosopher , Frank Martela, PhD (practising psychologist in Finland) on the topic “why the people of Finland are the happiest on the earth ? ” “lower income inequality (most importantly, the difference between the highest paid and the lowest paid), high social support, freedom to make decisions, and low levels of corruption”. These are found in many other developed western countries too.. These are the categories most often told by population analysts. But the psychologist added one important point. The Finns national image is being mostly introverts, quiet and a bit on melancholy types . This is contrary to being the happiest people in the world. So he attributes their cultural upbringing to their happiness. Their culture teaches them the following.. If you are happy hide it, do not show off. (humility pays) Being a pessimist helps you to face problems if any. (being better prepared) Your are the blacksmith of your own happiness, (do not base it on others) Be happy with what you have. “Some are happy, everyone has sunshine” is their common saying. (Contentment). .. He said “they are very humble”. They do not show off nor spite others. The Finns even if very rich still go around in simple small cars, wear simple clothes, have no peer pressure or peer neighbour pressure, own less material wealth and give more. They do not chase happiness. It happens indirectly to them. This is a big “positive “ revelation on a group of people living in quite harsh climatic conditions. In this world filled with cut-throat competitions , constant pressure to fulfill desires, addiction to new gadgets and accessories and always wanting change to better , this kind of humility and contentment is different and definitely an easy way to happiness . So happiness comes from Contentment and Humility. Try it out and feel light, peaceful and happy. 17.3.24

Question: How do hotels monitor guests bringing visitors to their rooms?
Answer: They watch.. The cameras watch, the staff incharge of cameras watches us, 24 hrs. The main gate watchmen, the janitor of the lobby and all staff at the reception. The slices were big spicy or whole fish like Catla, Rohu, anchovies, mackeral, jalebis just then fried on request . Who can resist that ? I was quickly tempted to buy 7 slices /Rs 100 of spicy, deep fried catla fish given to me wrapped in a news paper. It was sold by a roadside shop run by an old lady. Question: When you have guests over for lunch/dinner, do you serve buffet style or do you plate the food for them?
Answer: When we have guests more than 12 or more say 12 at a time then it is buffet. With one group sitting in the dining chairs and the rest, usually youngsters serving themselves and sitting in the hall or other rooms with tv on. We plate too if there are many of them or children. Sometimes ladies serve and go to the inner rooms or the sit out. Each of them helps themselves by coming to the buffet serve place for second or third helpings. Dessert is served in bowls later . Water, juice etc are already poured in glasses and kept. If the number is around 6 to 8 we sit together. Women serve the men first and then we sit too. The second helping is up the men to serve themselves by all passing the food bowls. But we chat, laugh and thus take longer time to finish. I love these as we get to talk to everyone heart to heart. People speak the truth when good food goes in. If it is a festival or a gathering at home with 24 or more say for mini - functions we all sit down in a line and food is served on banana leaves. The floor is cleaned, furniture pushed to the edges and clean sheets folded and spread in lines on either sides . The guests sit in a line, males and children first. Food is served on cleaned (water sprinkled and wiped) banana leaves. Food is served by women. Then the next batch sits. The last batch is us women. Then men come to serve us. The final group is the helpers, maids, cooks, drivers etc. We all serve them . A typical banana leaf spread of Tamizh food. 1.3.24.

Question: What are five things senior citizens should not do at the age of 65 and over?
Answer: I am not of that age, my husband is but moving with such people in my relatives and friends circle I have these to say Do not retire from life even if retired from your full time jobs. Take up easy jobs, if you want too. Take up hobbies, go shopping, watch tv, see movies, tour, talk to friends etc Have something as good time pass. This helps to keep your mind busy and happy. It keeps you physically fit too. Do not be in a hurry to divide and give away your property and wealth to your adult children. You can write a will though and keep it safe. Your adult children can earn their own money. Easy money has no value. Besides you giving them away is like giving away your self respect and your future security. Money in hand keeps you self reliant. Depending on children for money is a curse. Do not neglect yourself. Take care of your health. Take care your diet. Do simple exercises . Being mobile is a blessing. Go for walks. Do not complain about your various aches and pains. Nobody is interested nor willing to care for you. They do not have time for elder people care even if parents / inlaws Avoid unnecessary hospital visits. Do not give advice to anybody unless asked for. Even if they are going wrong let them learn from their mistakes. They will hate you for advising and only laugh at your advice. Besides they think they know everything thanks to Google, perplexity etc. Do not be over inquisitive about others’ lives. Never ask anyone personal questions. Avoid loose talk or giving suggestions to them (your adult children etc), on their increasing body weight, their gadget addiction, spending meaninglessly, not saving money, about not eating healthy food and how to care for their general health. Adult children hate these topics and see us as enemies or irritating / boring preachers ! But often mothers like me get away with such (harsh) advice because if we mothers don't tell then who will ? So talk to them and not about them. Do not idle away your time. Travel to keep yourself busy. Go on package tours well arranged by experienced travel agents....

Question: What do you do when you're home alone and out of toilet paper?

Question: How do people living alone keep their homes clean and tidy?
Answer: My friend’s fil lived alone in Trichy, Tamil Nadu. He had two sons, both married and they lived in Chennai. My friend pleaded with him to move in with them, Chennai after her mil passed away. But the old man felt very comfortable in his own house, with tenants, up and down floors. He had many life long friends and relatives in Trichy. He had a daily maid who kept the house clean and a cook who came twice to make food for him. He was a vegetarian and the cook was also a vegetarian, so cooked well according to his tastes. The maid and cook did most of the grocery shopping. Otherwise he hardly had any needs. He was a simple man. He also had a gardener to take care of the trees and shrubs in his compound. Any big issues were dealt by his sons like compound wall rebuilding, house painting or searching a new tenant etc. All other problems, were easily managed by him with just a phone call or word sent through the maid to the local plumber, shop keeper, his family doctor, electrician etc. He survived corona attack too. Question: Are barnacles good for anything?
Answer: Some people eat the barnacles. Barnacles are crustaceans not mulluscs as most people assume. They are related to crabs, lobsters and prawns. The only part that can be eaten is the meat located in the muscular stalk or "foot" of the barnacle, also known as the peduncle. Their taste has been described as similar to a very sweet razor clam, a mussel, or a cross between oysters and lobsters. Goose-neck barnacles are treated as delicacies in countries like Spain and Portugal. They are high-priced meat, going for as much as $500 per kilo. Its steep price is due to the danger and hard work that goes into harvesting these species from intertidal areas. Its chunky, muscular stalk is the most sought after part of a barnacle. Goose neck barnacles. Non edible small barnacles on rocks, Port Stephens, Australia. We visited this place as it is near Sydney. 14. 2.24
