Question: Can a person be forever alone? What are the chances of someone being forever alone if they have no friends or significant other?
Answer: Chances are quite high nowadays.. Now you can choose your life, whom to be with, whom to be without, whether you need family, siblings, friends, people or not. The last option of living in retirements homes with everything taken care of wasn't there some decades ago atleast in India, my country. But it gives people even more confidence to live alone, self reliant, stress free and happy. So if you think you can live alone, you can manage alone with whatever education, job, salary, money you earn, save, then go ahead. There are people who prefer being left alone although they may be the best of co workers, colleagues, family, siblings even neighbours etc. But in private they prefer being alone, not necessarily lonely. They may be happy with the freedom of time, space and relationships. With more and more families breaking, parents divorcing, relationships breaking up within family.. children in such families grow up very independent. They soon conclude it is not a must to continue a relationship or friendship. Another reason is the less hold parents have on adult children. Arranged marriages are losing out. Love marriages are failing. Friends are losing touch. Those around are betraying. So the net result is living alone as a single forever. Better safe than emotionally sorry. Children and teens, start living independently and get used to it. Soon they become adults who choose a life alone. They live alone in apartments once they have a good source of money , watch tv alone, eat alone, go out alone, spend holidays alone. They may even stop contacting parents and siblings. They may not report for festivals and family gatherings and go completely no contact and prefer that free happy life. A simple change of phone number or a leaving for job abroad helps people cut contacts from others. It is that easy. It is happier without any gives - takes, no obligations, no broken promises, no limits on anything. If you are healthy both mentally and physically you can manage alone. Otherwise you may find it difficult in times of trouble, depression, sickness and other misfortune. 14.2.24.

Question: Dating Advice in India: What should I do to prepare myself for my first night as an Indian couple?
Answer: Indian couple.. Hindu Indian couple Have a bath, wear fresh, comfortable clothes. If you are still in “cultural” dress change to them after the rituals soon after entering your bedroom, presuming you have an attached wash room. Remove all jewels, accessories and keep them away. Keep all gadgets away. Switch off ringing of phones. There are friendly crooks who may call or message you just to interrupt your special evening. Keep some soft music on to fill up any odd silence. It can even calm you. Drink the milk given or brought by the bride and have the sweets and fruits. The sweet - milk combination calms you. The serotonin in milk is a happy hormone. It makes you happy, satisfied and keeps you positive. This is essential on this day. Talk to each other as friends if it is an arranged marriage or as best friends if it is a love marriage. Talking eases the situation. Understanding each other is the first step to get closer to your spouse. Those used to a light, evening drink can take out your finest wine bottle and glasses for a happy start. If you both are tired and yawning away, go to sleep. The pre - wedding, morning wedding rituals, reception and feasts would have tired you out. It is OK to sleep and go slow with other matters. There is a life time out there for everything . Plan your honeymoon to somewhere which fits in your budget. Do not be too demanding. Do not expect parents or inlaws to sponsor the trip. Go away far for a few days, from everybody to enjoy each other's company and life together. 5.2.24

Question: What is the big deal about the Ram Temple in Ayodhya? There are so many Ram temples in the world. Why is there so much excitement and craze for this one?
Answer: There are many good and elaborate answers here by other writers. My explanation is very simple.. There is only one Jerusalem, only one Mecca, one Bodh gaya, one Mathura.. You cannot shift Jesus's birth place for your or history's convenience. It will lose its speciality, the holiness associated with it. Similarly for other places too. Similarly there is only one Ayodhya. This is the place Rama was born as per the Ramayana even if you call it as a folk tale. Rama was a real person, a hero as per our culture. He deserves his birthplace given back to him with full honours. Hence this temple which was there many years ago and destroyed by invaders has been rebuilt finally but this time on a larger scale, with a new idol. The former ancient idol is also retained. You travel the world, have jobs in different places, buy houses abroad.. Yet your birth place, your native town /village /city remains the same. You cannot say I spent 50 years abroad so I changed my birth place as per my convenience ! Here Rama is a a god for billions of Hindus. His birth place holds deep reverence and lots of importance for them. It is a pilgrimage centre with many Hindus wanting to visit this place atleast once in a lifetime like they visit Rameshwaram, Varanasi another such holy town for Hindus. Equate this with Jerusalem or Mecca. It will be easy to understand why this hype, this sense of satisfaction and achievement for all Hindus. And this rant about Rama and Sita not being important in southern parts of India is absolutely senseless and baseless. The map shows Rama temples in south India.. .besides the small ones not accounted Temple in Rameshwaram commonly called as Ramanathaswamy temple Rama halted in Rameshwaram prayed to Shiva, before leaving to Lanka. The Shiva temple with the Shivling built by Rama in Rameshwaram is equally important for all Hindus. Those in doubt visit Rameshwaram for first hand information on these proofs. Besides there are “N “number of Rama temples in all southern Indian States as shown in the above Google source. 26.1.24

Question: What could be the age of the Lord Rama depicted in the idol of the Ayodhya Rama temple?
Answer: The idol of Rama in the Ayodhya Rama temple is that of a 5 year old Rama as a child. The 51-inch idol (4ft 1/4 inches) , carved from black stone, was dressed in a yellow dhoti with a golden crown, necklaces, holding a golden bow and arrow. The idol is made up of black stone( black schist) in keeping with the colour of Rama as depicted in Ramayana, unlike the usual white marble stones used for idols in temples of Northern India. The idol is heavily jewelled to show Rama ‘s royal lineage. See the beautiful face, the lotus eyes and chubby cheeks of the 5 year old child idol. The idol was sculpted by a famous sculptor from Mysore.. Arun Yogiraj. "I feel I am the luckiest person on the earth now. The blessing of my ancestors, family members and Lord Ram Lalla has always been with me. Sometimes I feel like I am in a dream world...," Arun Yogiraj told news agency ANI. The idol carved by Yogiraj, now adorning the sanctum sanctorum of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, is made from a three-billion-year-old rock, according to a UGC-emeritus professor at the Department of Earth Sciences, University of Mysore. The rock known as "Krishna Shile" or black schist, was excavated from Gujjegowdanapura in H.D. Kote Taluk. Its smooth surface texture makes it an ideal choice for sculptors. It is a three billion year old metamorphic rock. 22.1.24

Question: What can be done to prevent "shaking" while trying to fall asleep?
Answer: The sudden twitching movement happens to few of us just before going into a deep sleep. It is an involuntary act probably caused by muscular contractions or by motor nerves. Doctors and scientists call this as a hypnic (or hypnagogic) or myoclonic jerk. A shake of legs is common, while full body jerk is seen too. It literally wakes us up and we have to try to go back to sleep once again. It is most irritating and happens once or twice normally before we go into a good sleep . It is harmless and usually cannot be prevented voluntarily. Hypnic jerks are associated with a rapid heartbeat, quickened breathing, sweat, and sometimes "a peculiar sensory feeling of 'shock' or 'falling into the void'". It can also be accompanied by a vivid dream experience or hallucination. Doctors suggest the following to prevent this sleep disturbing shakes by Drinking lots of water. Muscular dehydration is one main cause. Having B12 supplements Avoiding exercise just before hitting the bed. A minimum of 4 hours between sleep and exercise is good Having more vegetables, fruits rich in magnesium, calcium and iron. Avoid caffeine in coffee, colas, chocolates, cocoa drinks etc after 4pm if sleeping by 9pm. Avoid alcohol, drugs and nicotine . Have a light dinner. 21.1.24

Question: How do you say the words 'Tamil' and 'Tamizh' in the Tamil language?

Many non Thamizhians cannot say the letter zh as they are not trained with the various Thamizh alphabet. Nor is the letter zh ழ equivalent found in other languages except some like Malayalam. Even the young generation of Tamizh children and teens cannot say the letter zh and words that have zh ழ in them like pazham பழம், kizham கிழம் etc Hence they say Thamizh தமிழ் as thamil or Tamil. The zh ழ gets replaced by the English letter L. So Thamizh becomes tamil or தமில். So Thamizh is written as தமிழ். And Tamil is written as தமில். This word is wrong and not accepted by those who love the Thamizh language. 30.12.23

Question: Is it considered acceptable to take grandchildren out of school for a family vacation?
Answer: Depends on what grade they are in. In India 10th, 12 th grade students should attend school on all days so that they do not miss out on any important lessons, practice tests or practical work. They face public exams in these classes. Other class children taking a few days off is okay with permission from the school authorities and a proper reason.. Like a wedding in the family or reunion day. Simply going on a vacation for 10 days, when the school has just reopened after a long summer or winter vacation is never appreciated by teachers. 24.12.23

Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: My mom came from a family of 11 children. Why did she decide to have only one child?
Answer: Experience, struggle in childhood and teenage can change people's view on life. A relative of ours a pleasant, elderly lady has often expressed what a tough childhood, teenage and adult life she had as she was the eldest of 8 children.. 4 daughters, 4 sons. She was all the time taking care of her younger brothers and sisters right from her childhood years missing out on playtime and study time. She was fed up of seeing her mother getting a new baby every second year. It was a strain on the family economic condition too with only father earning. She missed out on her big share of parent’s love because there were so many babies. She was forced to cook and do other house hold work, at the expense of her higher education. This kind of responsibility on her tender shoulders made her so fed up that she decided she would go for a single child …she got a son so the question of second child never arose. ( This was in early 70s when having 3 children was a norm .) . She didn't want any more , even though her husband wanted, he being the only child in his family. He wanted a house filled with noise and children running around she expressed once.. She dreaded those years of struggle even in her senior years.

They feel a false pride and a sense of superiority if they are good in English or French as in India and Pondicherry. Then started the trend of the new hybrid language like Tanglish (Tamil and English) Hinglish (Hindi and English). Wherein native language and English are easily mixed up like a kichidi dish and spoken. This hybrid language is seen not only among school, college children, but also in young office goers, married couples etc These then speak only English to their children as a sign of advancement. Name: Bhuvana Rameshwar
Question: Smriti Irani opposed by menstrual paid leaves) what is your opinion?
Answer: During my work years in a Christian minority school in Ooty, India, we weren't allowed to take leave as we had proper summer and winter vacations besides very important festivals and national holidays . The rules were however different for different teachers. We Hindus were majority then. Hindus had to work on all days even if sick, child is sick or we had body pain etc. Even on Saraswathi (goddess of knowledge) pooja day we had to conduct drawing and handwriting competitions ! Books, studies, writing notes are left as they are to be worshipped on this day . Many of us too had abdominal cramps on our ‘three days’ yet never spoke of it to others, neither at home nor in place of work . Maybe a few friends, knew our discomfort. Most of us were used to it as it comes every month and felt better with some physical activity, out of home. Christians, Muslims teachers however would take leave on their fast days (lent, ramadan) , festivals, visit to holy places like vellankanni / dargahs and one or two days, with full rights for menstrual pain. It was understood if some teacher is absent without informing, every month. Soon all new teachers learnt the trick. They took off to go on a date, go for some personal bank work, purchases to nearby big cities, meet somebody out of Ooty town, avoid sports day practice, annual day preparation etc and give “periods cramps ” as the leave letter reason. Most of us seniors weren't smart enough that way. So this law can be misused. All it needs is a woman somehow working those three days (or resting in the place of work) and taking leave some other day, in the same month for better reasons other than the actual periods rest. 22.12 23.

Nearby yet separate and have their own place. If your spouse isn't happy with this especially the expense , move them in, give them their own room with a tv. Send them food etc on time. Visit them in their room. Last option stay with them and visit your spouse. 😅. A walk -friend (in his 40s ) of my husband relocated to Bangalore from Chicago (US ) as his senior parents needed him. Last he heard from our common friends.. he is divorced and past three years remarried and happy. 20.12.23

Question: Is it necessary to soak moong dal overnight before eating it? If not, how long should it be soaked for?

Question: I want to go on a vacation with my husband but he won’t go on vacation without his parents and sister’s family. What does this mean?
Answer: I would call this as “ joint family “ syndrome. This affects not only men, women too. Everytime they want to go on a holiday they feel it is basic etiquettes to invite other family members too like senior parents, uncles, aunts, who live with them, married sister and her family etc. This is because in earlier years the parents hardly went on any vacation. So every place young adults plan to go isn't seen by others. Hence this obligation. So now the men /women are too shy or scared to go alone with their wife /husband and children. They feel it is selfish to do so. The guilt will kill the holiday fun. They may become grumpy too spoil their spouse's happiness also. There were times when people in joint families would get upset if a newly married couple went on a honeymoon or any holiday without others. But now things have changed. Adult children only inform and leave with no invitation to parents or others. Parents are also decent enough to refuse even if invited, knowing it is only namesake. But they do plan another family outing with seniors, unmarried siblings, married siblings, and families as an annual family get together. So initially plan one for yourself as a couple and then one with everybody else as a family get-together. Thus alternate such trips. Soon he will realise taking everybody isn't as easy, enjoyable and budget friendly as going away as a couple with your own child /children. 16.12.23

Scientifically if we sleep at odd hours we miss out mingling with others, feel lazy to have tea and snacks and sulk at dinner time being still sleepy. Question: In India, when people go out to eat at a restaurant, why do they usually order their own dish instead of sharing with others at the table?
Answer: When we order Indian breakfast items they are usually served just enough for one person /plate. So we do not share idlies, bread - omelette, chapathis, pooris, plain dosa, masala dosa, vadas, upma, rava dosa, rava kichidi. But when we ask for the second breakfast item then sometimes we share half dosa or one poori, one chapathi with others including the sambar, veg kurma or white peas gravy. But in non veg hotel when we order different biryanis it is served individually or if it is a big family of children, adults and seniors food is shared by keeping it in a bowl in the centre. Usually such people order “family biryani ” or bucket biryani and 3 or 4 side dishes. This is shared among 6 or 8 people depending on their eating capacity. But if friends order different biryanis then it is not shared. So are south Indian or north Indian meals . They are not shared. But we always share Chinese dishes. Even we have a concept of dividing 1 by 2 the soups in Chinese, Thai restaurants. Similarly eats and starters are always shared in most restaurants.

Question: Which is better on holidays, a travel vacation or a family reunion?
Answer: I have had both the above in our vacation days. When in laws were alive we gathered every vacation.. Parents inlaw, all brothers and sisters and their families. My fil made sure we all attended, gathered at home but we went on some out of town visits sometimes temples sometime seashore with packed food. Sometimes we also had family reunions in some nearby holiday spots like our default vacation spot mammalapuram. Sea bath, sea food, lots chatting, playing in the beach was real fun. There was fun but those living far away had to make travel arrangements well in advance. Get togethers at homes meant feast, more work for women especially those good in cooking and those younger in age. The others chatted, asking for hourly snacks, tea, juice etc. By the end of the trip we hurriedly packed our bags and rushed to the railway station, all tired mentally and physically with thoughts of the journey back home and the monotonous routine life once again. The family reunion trip was fun for children as they got to meet cousins, relatives and a happy one for the grandparents. But I somehow felt too tired mentally as we were invariably subjected to lots of gossip, complaints and family politics. Some misunderstandings too would crop up. It was very obvious that the smart ones neither worked nor helped out with the expenditure. But those were days when people had respect for parents /parents inlaw. But now with them dead we do not enjoy those fake family get togethers much. We attend one or two per year may be as family weddings or some birthday party. But now the number of inland tours and foreign trips have increased . These are more fun. Not much work as stay, travel and food are all taken care off . In my family we are all travel buffs. So the enjoyment is more. We learn more about known places and get to see new places too. Each place is a new learning… in science, architecture, history, political views geography, new cities , new culture, new food, new people.. The list is endless. Photography is our passion too. So anytime I choose vacation travel over family get togethers. 13.12.23

Question: I'm a topper in my college but my roommate, the only one whom I believe so much, gets jealous of me. How can I react to this situation?
Answer: Congrats on being a college topper. Your reaction to others jealousy can be by being blind, deaf and dumb to it . Humans show jealousy, envy, anger and hatred. You are above human if you are able to ignore these things in others. Laugh to yourself if you see envy around you. We all may feel jealous of others sometimes. But there is no need to show it out and spoil relationships. A good human keeps all these negative emotions in control. And soon comes out of it with only a positive outlook everywhere. So if your best friend /room mate /classmate /relative / even sibling is jealous of you, start giving them lesser information about you hereafter. Do not talk about your goals, the process, your achievements etc. Much as you desperately want someone to share this joy, keep them to yourself. No point making others feel jealousy and hatred towards you lest they start harming you, your good name and your progressive activities. Only achievers know this pain. I have been in such situations in my life too. Friends turning into foes, cousins foul mouthing you and relatives spreading defaming rumours..these were common in my college years. Initially it hurts. But soon we learn to face this crap. So keeping your goals, achievements unknown to others applies not only in student life but right upto senior years. Nobody is happy with your progress and your happiness. Live your life and let them see. Do not talk about it. Have the last laugh, that too secretly. Life's like that.. 😃 12.12.23

Question: Is there an obligation for a person to care for their unborn child's health before birth?
Answer: Yes. Because the unborn baby didn't ask you to give birth to it. You decided to have this baby. If so take care of its growth every day, every week, every month until delivery. You wanted it to be born on this earth so it is your moral obligation to let it be born as a physically and mentally fit baby, who grows up equally fit in later years. Keep off alcohol, smoking and drugs for the good health of this helpless foetus. Even simple medicines like painkillers, anti vomit, sleep inducers can harm your child. Life is often very difficult even for a well formed, normal baby and later an adult. So imagine life of a child if it is born physically or mentally challenged. It could be life long torture for no fault of his/her. Here is a list of the common disorders caused by pregnant mothers drinking, smoking, doing drugs, taking “over the counter” medicines, not being on a good diet, being stressed and mentally unhappy. Cleft palate Heart, bone and kidney problems Spina bifida Deformed bodies.. Lack of hands or legs, vision and hearing problems Mental disabilities Genital problems Too small babies with low birth weight, small head, not fully developed body People with FAS (fetal alcohol syndrome) have central nervous system (CNS) problems, minor facial features, and growth problems. They also have problems with learning, memory, attention span, communication, vision or hearing. So please take care during your pregnancy months. Eat healthy and take all your vitamins and minerals supplements by consulting your doctor. Do not give birth to a child who is challenged in any way. If you are an unfit , uncaring, no - time mother better you prevent conception or abort if it was an unwanted pregnancy. 12.12.23

Question: We don't live for ourselves; our society, family, friends & job/business get 98% of our attention, time & efforts. Out of 24 hours, how many hours do you allocate for your personal growth & happiness?
Answer: Let's divide this into three parts in our adult life Before marriage.. Most of the time what I did was for my happiness be it as studies, with friends,, eating different types of food, with stress relievers like entertainment, shopping, chatting, dressing up for college, sports etc. So me time for happiness was more. There were no politics, no manipulations no unhealthy competition or any sort of jealousy. . It was a carefree life. Best of the lot too. We had almost the whole of 24 hours as ours minus the restful sleep time. Some enjoyed that too chatting with friends late night. We have lots of friends in all directions. They give us hope of a happy future together. We dream big and jot out many plans. After marriage.. Here come in family, responsibity, saying yes to extended family, fearing society, working tirelessly at home and outside, working for family. Here life keeps moving with no control as if we are standing in a crowded street, people keep shoving you to whichever side the crowd moves. Here time is not for us . It is for family, children, society and others. We spend a lot of time in working and earning money. Only time that is for our happiness is sleep (rest) time say 6 to 8 hours . We have no time to exercise and do not pay attention to our diet and health. Birthdays and anniversaries fly by with or without celebration. We lose many of our friends, most with regrets and some just disappear. And before you know middle age crosses by and we head towards our senior years with only a handful of people close to us . We are at the peak of career with no time, no friends and genuine happiness. After retiring from regular jobs. Time is all ours. Adult children leave the house to make their own nests. Our duties, our hard working years are now over. We are relaxed without any tension or any time bars. Time is now at our disposal. It is completely up to us to use time for our own happiness. Sleep too reduces to 6 hrs maximum. That leaves almost 18 hours only for personal happiness, passions, hobbies,entertainment, travels, tours, friends, social causes, books etc. Earlier cooking was a chore now it is an art. Exercise is no more a bore, it becomes an excuse to enjoy nature, meet friends. What remains are the best of relatives and friends. Most others have left for reasons known to time. Time is all ours now provided we choose happiness above all our past decisions, regrets and shortcomings. 9.12.23.

Question: What is the importance of Sambar powder in South Indian cuisine? What will happen if it's missing from our kitchen shelves?
Answer: Sambar powder is used for all types of sambars, non dhal gravies, veg fries and sea food gravies and fries. If sambar powder is missing from our shelf we can make one easily at home by dry frying red chilies, coriander seeds, little yellow gram, little black gram, cumin seeds, pepper corns, fenugreek seeds, curry leaves, fried asafoetida, cooling them and then dry grinding them together. For ratios.. check a cookery book or online recipe. Or wet grinding them in a small mixie. For sambar used for serving with idkues, dosa, pongal, vada etc grind some roast coconut pieces for that extra flavour. Also grind it slightly coarser. Suppose you do not have time then what to do for that day’s sambar making. Simple.. add two table sp of coriander powder, two tbsp of chilly powder, 1/4 tea spoon of cumin powder, 1/4 tea spoon of pepper powder, 1/4 tsp of turmeric powder, 1/4 tea spoon of asafoetida in a bowl. Mix well and keep. Use this as instant sambar powder. For tempering use a little medium hot oil.. Fry in it mustard seeds, a few broken red chillies, cumin seeds, a little fenugreek and curry leaves. Sambar smells excellent. 6.12.23
